findings.findingDescription: Leaky abstraction: Endpoint returns internal database entity [ActivityLog] without DTO encapsulation
causalTrace: 1. Controller method returns raw database @Entity instead of decoupled DTO.
2. Internal schema columns, audit fields, and relationship graphs are exposed over HTTP.
3. API clients bind to internal database representations, creating tight coupling.
4. Callers can exploit over-posting / mass-assignment by modifying internal entity fields.
findings.groundTruthEvidence: ActivityLog is an annotated JPA database persistence entity (@Entity, @Table(name = 'activity_logs') in ActivityLog.java). AdminAuditController.getSystemPulse directly returns List<ActivityLog> from activityRepo.findAllByOrderByTimestampDesc() without DTO mapping, exposing internal audit fields and schema details. Verified True Positive (TP).
findings.reviewerNotes: Successfully resolved via cross-file entity resolution. Patch deferred to multi-file refactoring planner.

findings.findingDescription: Path Traversal vulnerability in Path.get() call
causalTrace: 1. StudentController.uploadPhoto(id)
2. fileName = "profile_" + id + ".png"
3. Paths.get("src/main/resources/static/images/" + fileName)
4. File system resolves path outside the intended base directory.
findings.groundTruthEvidence: fileName is constructed as 'profile_' + id + '.png' where id is @PathVariable Long id. In Spring Web MVC, Long parameters are strongly typed and parsed as numerical values; arbitrary directory traversal sequences ('../') cannot match the route or parse as Long, failing with TypeMismatchException / 400 Bad Request. The taint engine treated Long id as a tainted String. Verified False Positive (FP).
findings.reviewerNotes: Engine taint analysis lacks type-aware source filtering for numeric path variables (Long/Integer).

findings.findingDescription: Path Traversal vulnerability in Path.get() call
causalTrace: 1. StudentController.uploadResume(file)
2. fileName = System.currentTimeMillis() + "_" + file.getOriginalFilename()
3. Paths.get(uploadDir + fileName)
4. File system resolves path outside the intended base directory.
findings.groundTruthEvidence: file.getOriginalFilename() is directly extracted from untrusted client-controlled HTTP Content-Disposition headers. An attacker can submit filenames containing directory traversal sequences (e.g. '../../malicious.sh'), allowing arbitrary file writes outside uploads/resumes/. No Path.normalize() or startsWith(baseDir) containment check exists. Verified True Positive (TP).
findings.reviewerNotes: High-risk Arbitrary File Write (CWE-22 / CWE-73). Genuine real-world security vulnerability.

findings.findingDescription: Path Traversal vulnerability in Path.get() call
causalTrace: 1. User provides relative path payload with '../' sequence.
2. Path is concatenated into File / Path object without canonicalization (.normalize()).
3. File system resolves path outside the intended base directory.
4. Sensitive system or tenant file is accessed or overwritten.
findings.groundTruthEvidence: Target path is constructed from constant uploadDir ('src/main/resources/static/images/') and hardcoded filename 'signature.png'. No user input flows into the path constructor. Verified False Positive (FP).
findings.reviewerNotes: Engine flagged Paths.get sink because method accepts MultipartFile, but the actual path string contains only literals.

findings.findingDescription: Path Traversal vulnerability in File instantiation
causalTrace: 1. EmailNotificationService.sendJobApplication(resumePath)
2. new File(resumePath)
3. File system resolves path outside the intended base directory.
findings.groundTruthEvidence: Service method sendJobApplication accepts resumePath directly and instantiates new File(resumePath) without path containment verification. Because resumePath originates from user-uploaded filenames, this enables arbitrary local file reading and attachment to outgoing emails. Verified True Positive (TP).

findings.findingDescription: Non-deterministic java.util.Random instantiation in business service
causalTrace: 1. Business service method invokes global system time or unseeded random generator.
2. Method behavior cannot be frozen, simulated, or deterministically tested across environments.
3. Test suites suffer from intermittent flakiness depending on execution clock.
4. Time-dependent edge cases (leap seconds, timezone shifts) remain unverified.
findings.groundTruthEvidence: EmailNotificationService is a Spring @Service generating authentication OTP verification codes using unseeded java.util.Random(). Direct instantiation of Random in business services violates deterministic testability and introduces predictable pseudo-random OTPs (CWE-330). Verified True Positive (TP).

findings.findingDescription: Leaky abstraction: Endpoints in EventController, InternshipController, PartnerController return JPA entities without DTO encapsulation
findings.groundTruthEvidence: A total of 16 endpoint instances exposing JPA database entities across 6 controllers were missed: EventController (getAllEvents line 31, createEvent line 35, getRegisteredStudents line 43), InternshipController (getAllInternships line 25, createInternship line 34, searchBySkills line 43, getInternshipApplicants line 75), PartnerController (registerPartner line 64, getPendingPartners line 93, getWatchlist line 138, addToWatchlist line 151), AdminAuditController (getPendingAudits line 36, getAllPartners line 79), AuthController (registerStudent line 46), and WalletController (syncWallet line 45, addExperience line 50). Across all 8 controllers, 22 endpoints expose JPA entities. SentinelPR missed these 16 findings because ArchitectureReviewEngine.matchesFqcn() constructed candidate FQCN as 'candidatePkg + "." + simpleName', causing the first candidate in the package ('ActivityLog') to falsely match every explicit import in com.scc.smart_campus.model and return false when checking for JPA annotations. Verified False Negative (FN).
findings.reviewerNotes: Engine defect identified in ArchitectureReviewEngine.matchesFqcn(): Candidate class name must be checked against simpleName or candidate.getPrimaryClassName(). Observation recorded; fix deferred per Phase 4A.6 policy.

findings.findingDescription: Fail-open security block inspection across services and controllers
findings.groundTruthEvidence: All try-catch blocks return error responses (e.g. 500 / 400) or throw RuntimeException. No catch blocks silently swallow security exceptions or grant bypass access. Evaluated safe.

findings.findingDescription: I/O stream lifecycle and resource management inspection
findings.groundTruthEvidence: All I/O operations utilize Spring MVC managed multipart streaming or Files.copy which closes underlying streams. No unclosed raw FileInputStream/FileOutputStream or socket descriptors exist. Evaluated safe.

findings.findingDescription: Concurrency and volatile field inspection across services and models
findings.evidence: private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, String> otpCache = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
findings.groundTruthEvidence: Zero volatile field declarations exist in the entire codebase. Shared in-memory caches utilize ConcurrentHashMap rather than unsafe volatile compound operations. Evaluated safe.

findings.findingDescription: Subprocess execution inspection across business logic
findings.groundTruthEvidence: Zero ProcessBuilder or Runtime.getRuntime().exec() invocations exist in the repository. Evaluated safe.

findings.findingDescription: SQL query execution and ORM query composition inspection
findings.evidence: public interface StudentRepository extends JpaRepository<Student, Long>
findings.groundTruthEvidence: All database operations strictly utilize Spring Data JpaRepository built-in methods and derived finder queries (e.g. findByEmail, findByStatus). No raw SQL string concatenation, EntityManager.createNativeQuery, or JDBC Statement calls exist. Hibernate parameter binding enforces parameterized queries. Evaluated safe.

findings.findingDescription: Object deserialization and stream serialization inspection
findings.groundTruthEvidence: All request payload deserialization is performed by Jackson JSON parser via Spring Web MVC @RequestBody. Zero Java native ObjectInputStream.readObject() calls exist in the project. Evaluated safe.

findings.findingDescription: Hardcoded secret and credential entropy inspection
findings.groundTruthEvidence: All sensitive credentials in application.properties reference environment variables (${SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD}, ${MAIL_PASSWORD}) or non-secret template placeholders ([YOUR-PASSWORD]). Java source files contain zero API tokens, AWS keys, or private certificates. Evaluated safe.

findings.findingDescription: Spring Security CSRF configuration inspection
findings.groundTruthEvidence: Repository does not configure Spring Security and contains no SecurityFilterChain bean disabling CSRF protection. Evaluated safe.

findings.findingDescription: Spring CORS origin policy inspection
findings.groundTruthEvidence: WebConfig explicitly restricts allowed origins to designated development client ports (localhost:5503, 5505, 5506). No wildcard ('*') origin is configured with allowCredentials(true). Evaluated safe.

findings.findingDescription: Architectural layering and circular dependency inspection
findings.groundTruthEvidence: Class dependency graph forms an acyclic layered hierarchy (Controller -> Service -> Repository -> Model). No circular package or reciprocal class dependencies exist. Evaluated safe.

notes: Validation conducted as part of SentinelPR Phase 4A.6 real-repository evaluation on Smart Campus Connect (SSC-BACKEND).
Repository cloned into isolated scratch directory outside SentinelPR workspace (commit 2ab5c482e3a7fed2a0440ff27c247cdf0a9bec04).
Static AST and dataflow inspection completed without runtime code execution or database connection.
SentinelPR identified 11 total findings across ARCH-002 (6), SEC-006 (4), and ARCH-003 (1).
Human ground-truth verified 9 True Positives, 2 False Positives (SEC-006 on numeric path variable and literal filename), and 10 True Negatives across safe rules.

Identified an engine defect in ArchitectureReviewEngine.matchesFqcn() causing False Negatives for ARCH-002 when multiple classes share the same package. Defect identified and preserved per Phase 4A.6 observation-only policy.

Phase 4A.8 Post-Fix Validation: Following candidate class-identity matching fix in ArchitectureReviewEngine.matchesFqcn(), all 16 previously missed ARCH-002 endpoint instances are resolved and detected (22/22 ARCH-002 TP, 0 FN). SEC-006 remains unchanged at 4 findings (2 TP, 2 FP). Total findings: 27.
